points.description: States that variables can be declared anywhere in a program (not restricted to one fixed location).
points.partial_credit: Half marks if only one location is given as an example without saying declaration is possible anywhere.

points.description: States precisely that variables can be declared inside a function, and names these as local variables.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if inside a function is stated but 'local variables' is not named (or vice versa).

points.description: States precisely that variables can be declared outside all functions, and names these as global variables.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if outside functions is stated but 'global variables' is not named (or vice versa).

rubric.notes: Full marks need all three elements: declaration anywhere, inside functions as local variables, and outside functions as global variables, with the correct terms. Part marks only when clearly more than half of a point is precise. Vague answers (e.g. 'at the top') or any wrong statement about a point earn nothing for that point; a wrong location, such as 'only in main', loses the related point.
